clue.text: Opener to name one or two flats, perhaps

blocks.note: a key is what opens a lock
your signature is your name written by hand

explanation.surface: An estate agent's first job is to list a couple of apartments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flats' look like apartments, but they are musical flats: a key signature at the start of a stave shows which notes are flattened.
explanation.definitionFit: A key signature of one or two flat symbols tells the musician the piece is in F or B-flat major, for example.

clue.text: Affectionate Russian relatives

blocks.note: kind and affectionate both mean warm-hearted
Red was the standard label for a Soviet Russian

explanation.surface: A description of a warm-hearted family from Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred, used as a plural noun, means one's family members, the people related to you by blood.

clue.text: Gets out in the county

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, to yorker a batsman is to bowl them out with a ball pitched at their feet
second meaning: the usual short form of Yorkshire, a large county in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone escapes and ends up in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: A yorker is a cricket delivery that lands right at the batsman's feet; the verb means to dismiss someone with one.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorks is the standard abbreviation for Yorkshire, and to yorker means to dismiss a batsman in cricket.

clue.text: A guru in LA moving to an address in Washington

definitions.note: the answer is used as a noun here, short for inaugural address

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift out of their places and settle in a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles spiritual teacher relocates to the American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US 'an inaugural' is a noun: the speech a new president gives at the swearing-in in Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: Each new American president delivers an inaugural speech on taking office, so the noun names that Washington speech.

clue.text: Climbing plant without a fastening device

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the plant goes on with something left off
in a down entry, climbing means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests
taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A climbing plant that grows without any support pinned to it.
explanation.walkthrough: LIANA loses its final A to leave LIAN, which climbs up the grid to read NAIL. 'Climbing plant' looks like one phrase, but the plant alone is the liana.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail is a small metal spike hammered in to hold pieces of wood or other material together.

clue.text: Young person to generate trouble

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so these letters are stirred up into another order

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The stereotype of a youngster who stirs up bother.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone aged thirteen to nineteen counts as a teenager, an adolescent between childhood and adulthood.

clue.text: Proper set up, with great potential

blocks.note: to rig something is to set it up or fit it out
HT stands for high tension, a large electrical potential difference

explanation.surface: A well-organised venture full of promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potential' looks like promise, but it is electrical: high tension (HT) means high voltage.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and proper both describe what is correct, suitable or fitting for the occasion.

clue.text: Girl in taxi is using it for a trip

definitions.note: a description of the drug rather than a straight synonym

indicators.note: in places the girl's name inside the word for the vehicle

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
a common girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman in a taxi is taking it to go on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'trip' is a journey by cab; in the definition it is the drug sense, a high.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is slang for a drug-induced high, and cannabis is a drug people take to get one.

clue.text: Finally arrange to make payment

blocks.note: first meaning: to resolve or fix something conclusively
second meaning: to pay off a bill or debt

explanation.surface: At last sorting things out so that a bill can be paid.
explanation.definitionFit: You settle a dispute when you resolve it for good, and you settle a bill when you pay it.

clue.text: Royal turncoat found in simple story

indicators.note: found in says the royal traitor is discovered inside the word for simple

blocks.note: R stands for rex or regina, king or queen
a rat is someone who deserts their side
naive means simple or unsophisticated

explanation.surface: A plain tale about a traitor in the royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, a story told in sequence.

clue.text: A king — one in favour

blocks.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is the cipher of a King George
an ace is the one in a suit of cards

explanation.surface: A monarch and one of his courtiers enjoying royal favour.
explanation.walkthrough: GR stands for King George, as seen on British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace and favour both mean goodwill or kindness given freely, as in a royal grace-and-favour home.

clue.text: Padre's ignoble part in surrender

indicators.note: part says only a section of the words that follow is taken

blocks.note: the letters run across the apostrophe and the word break

explanation.surface: A chaplain plays a shameful role in a capitulation.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up or yield, as when a chess player concedes the game.

clue.text: A flyer starting elementary training requires strict disciplinarian

indicators.note: starting points to the opening letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A pilot beginning basic flight school needs a tough instructor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests an airman; here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet insists on rigid obedience to rules, named after a famously strict French army drillmaster.

clue.text: Withdraw from French sector

blocks.note: de is French for from
a sector is a part or section

explanation.surface: Pulling troops out of the French zone.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart and to withdraw both mean to leave or go away from a place.

clue.text: Ending voluntary support sounds indecent

indicators.note: sounds says the answer is heard as two other words when spoken

blocks.note: a post is an upright support
lewd means indecent

explanation.surface: Withdrawing backing that was freely given seems obscene.
explanation.walkthrough: A voluntary is an organ piece played in church; the postlude is the one played as the congregation leaves. 'Ending voluntary support' looks like stopping charity.
explanation.definitionFit: An organist plays a closing voluntary after a church service, and the formal term for that concluding piece is a postlude.

clue.text: Note bound to be of sound quality

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
liable means bound or obliged by law

explanation.surface: A musical note certain to have a good tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' suggests audio, but here it means solid and dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sound is trustworthy and dependable, so a thing of sound quality can be relied upon.

clue.text: Rigid code in Castile

indicators.note: putting words into code scrambles them, so the letters come out in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A strict set of laws in force in the old Spanish kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Castile is a historic kingdom in central Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inelastic does not stretch or give, so it is stiff and unbending.

clue.text: A giver, for example, in distress

indicators.note: the letters are in distress, upset and thrown out of order, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
e.g. is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: A generous donor finds themselves in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distress' does two jobs: with 'in' it tells you the letters are upset, and on its own it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve someone is to cause them pain or a sense of injustice, to trouble or upset them.

clue.text: Alcohol mixture with mature body

blocks.note: fusel oil is a mixture of higher alcohols formed in fermentation
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A blended drink with a full, ripe body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' sounds like a wine-taster's word; it is the body of an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuselage is the main central structure of an aeroplane, holding crew and passengers, its body.

clue.text: Iron lady's headgear?

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a lady's name; the 's links it to what follows

explanation.surface: A hint at what the Iron Lady, Margaret Thatcher, wore on her head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' was Margaret Thatcher's nickname, but the two words split into a chemical symbol and a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown and a brim, so it is a piece of headgear.

clue.text: Working the old way — in agreement

indicators.note: in puts the word for way inside the word for agreement

blocks.note: ye is the old way of writing the
ay is a form of aye, yes
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Doing a job in the traditional manner, and everyone agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' means fermenting, as beer or dough works when the yeast is active.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer or bread dough that is working is fermenting, frothy with active yeast, so it is yeasty.

clue.text: Christmas brand of record you'll hear first

indicators.note: hear says the word is to be judged by how it is spoken
first fixes the order, putting the spoken part ahead of the other piece

blocks.note: you'll is said like this old word for Christmas
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A seasonal make of record that you will listen to before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' puts the sound-alike part before the record. A brand is a burning piece of wood, not a make.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is a burning log, and the yule log is the big one traditionally burned at Christmas.

clue.text: State in Spain or Italy of alert

blocks.note: del means of the in both Spanish and Italian
alert and aware both mean watchful

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean country put on high alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware, on the east coast, was the first of the original colonies to ratify the US Constitution, making it a state.

clue.text: Catherine, perhaps, ends the stanza

blocks.note: first meaning: the spinning firework named after St Catherine, who was tortured on one
second meaning: in verse, the short set of rhyming lines closing a stanza

explanation.surface: Catherine finishes a verse of the poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catherine, perhaps' asks for something that can come before a Catherine wheel. 'Ends' is a verb here: the wheel finishes a stanza, as in Sir Gawain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catherine wheel is a type of rotating firework, and in prosody the short refrain closing a stanza bears the same name.

clue.text: The foreign crowd returned to wave

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in the other direction

blocks.note: le is French for the
to cram is to crowd or pack in

explanation.surface: An overseas mob came back to greet someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' looks like a greeting; it is a hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A marcel is a deep, regular wave set in the hair with heated tongs, named after a French hairdresser.

clue.text: Animal caught by soldiers on both sides of the Atlantic

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

blocks.clueFragment: soldiers on both sides of the Atlantic
blocks.note: OR, other ranks, are British soldiers and GIs are American ones, from either side of the ocean

explanation.surface: A creature captured by British and American troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a small short-legged Welsh dog breed, an animal famously kept by the Queen.

clue.text: It's known to everyone, said Jingle

definitions.note: a reference to Jingle's line rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: in Scots, the past participle of ken, to know
second meaning: the English county that Alfred Jingle in Dickens's Pickwick Papers says everybody knows

explanation.surface: A Dickens character declares something to be common knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Pickwick Papers the con man Jingle says 'Kent, sir, everybody knows Kent; apples, cherries, hops and women.' Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots speakers say kent for knew or known, and Dickens's Jingle claims everybody knows this southern English county.

clue.text: Midnight excursion around the hog's-back

indicators.note: the middle of night is its central letter
around says the trip word surrounds the selected letter

blocks.note: a ride is a short trip out
the central letter of the five

explanation.surface: A trip in the dead of night out along a hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: A hog's-back is a long, steep-sided hill; the Hog's Back is one in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: A hog's-back is a narrow hill crest shaped like a pig's back, which is a ridge.

clue.text: College to choose in the USA

definitions.text: College to choose in the USA
definitions.note: the answer is the adjective that completes the phrase

blocks.note: surface reading: picking a university to go to in America
setter's reading: the American body of delegates that chooses the president

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the word that goes before 'College' to name the body that formally elects the American president.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans vote for electors, and the Electoral College then formally picks the president and vice-president.

clue.text: Literary lady's luck begins to change

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so these letters take a different order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A writer's fortunes start to turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluestocking is a dated, often mocking term for a learned or intellectual woman, from an 18th-century literary circle.
